Action Plan:
1) Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
2) Arrange an in-person, face-to-face clinic evaluation in Central London with a GP to perform a full neurological examination and ENT/ear evaluation today, to confirm or exclude Bell’s palsy and to assess for other causes of unilateral left hearing loss with facial numbness (e.g., acoustic schwannoma/vestibular schwannoma, labyrinthitis). The exam will include hearing assessment and inspection of the ear.
3) Administrative booking: The admin team will schedule the appointment in Central London; patient to contact the support line after five minutes to be slotted into a convenient clinic address/time.
4) Treatment plan: No specific pharmacologic therapy documented at this time; management will be determined after the physical examination.
5) COVID-19 vaccine suitability: not applicable based on current information.
   
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Left-sided hearing loss with numbness of the left face for about 3 weeks; occasional tinnitus; intermittent dizziness.
- Onset, duration, progression: Onset ~3 weeks ago; persistent symptoms up to present.
- Laterality: Unilateral with left-sided symptoms (hearing loss and facial numbness around the left jaw/ear).
- Associated symptoms: No ear discharge, no ear pain, no fever, no weakness, no dysphagia, no vision changes reported.
- Other ENT history: Past nasal polyps; prior episode of labyrinthitis (not ongoing); uses nasal spray PRN; Rennies PRN.
- Medications: Nasal spray PRN (name not documented); Rennies PRN.
- Allergies: Latex.
- Past medical history: Nasal polyps; prior labyrinthitis; no chronic illnesses stated beyond these.
- Social history: Jockey by occupation; currently training reduced due to symptoms; lives with partner; lives alone in terms of residence with partner; no pets.
- Family history: Brother with Neurofibromatosis (NF).
- Other notes: Expressed concern about seriousness; sought reassurance; clinician discussed the plan for in-person assessment to clarify diagnosis.

Objective:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Physical exam: Not performed in this virtual visit; no objective findings recorded (ear exam and full neuro exam planned for in-person assessment).
- Focused findings to confirm on exam: Left unilateral hearing loss with left facial sensory involvement; tinnitus; episodic dizziness reported historically; no documented facial weakness or other cranial nerve deficits at this visit.
- Medications/Allergies: Latex allergy noted.
- Investigations/Imaging: none performed to date.

Assessment & Plan:
1) Issue 1: Left-sided unilateral hearing loss with facial numbness (left) plus tinnitus and dizziness
- Working diagnosis (likely diagnosis per transcript): Bell’s palsy considered as a possibility; not yet confirmed. DDx supports Bell’s palsy as a potential diagnosis (Likelihood: Medium).
- Differential diagnoses (from DDx consistent with transcript):
  - Acoustic schwannoma / vestibular schwannoma (Likelihood: Medium-High) — unilateral SNHL with tinnitus and dizziness; NF family history increases concern.
  - Labyrinthitis / vestibular neuritis (Likelihood: Medium) — unilateral hearing loss with tinnitus and dizziness; prior labyrinthitis history supports this possibility.
  - CPA tumors (vestibular schwannoma / meningioma) as part of the same spectrum (Likelihood: Low to Medium) — aligns with unilateral SNHL and dizziness; family history NF raises interest.
  - Bell’s palsy (idiopathic facial nerve palsy) (Likelihood: Medium) — considered in conversation; may explain facial numbness/sensory involvement, though weakness is typically present.
  - Vertebrobasilar insufficiency / posterior circulation ischemia (Likelihood: Low) — possible with dizziness and unilateral sensory symptoms but less likely given duration and lack of focal deficits.
- Investigations planned: In-person neurological examination today; ENT/ear examination; look inside the ear; no imaging ordered at this time but further workup may be guided by exam findings.
- Treatment planned: Not documented today; plan depends on exam findings (to confirm or exclude Bell’s palsy and other etiologies).
- Referrals: In-person clinic assessment in Central London with a GP/neurology exam and ENT evaluation today.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: No vital signs available; no documented physical examination findings yet; no lab/imaging results yet; exact medication names for the nasal spray not documented.
- Internal conflicts: No conflicts detected between transcript and DDx (no statements contradicted).
- Transcript quality: Video consult; some lines semi-inaudible; overall sufficient to form a plan, but lacks objective exam data until in-person assessment.

Notes for follow-up:
- Ensure attendance for same-day in-person neuro/ENT assessment in Central London; completion of a full neurological exam and ear inspection to confirm Bell’s palsy versus alternative etiologies.
- If imaging or audiology testing becomes indicated after examination, arrange accordingly.
